posts.raw_content:
It's hard. I'm still here though. To quote one of my favorite songs "I'm awful nice but I'm cold as ice; I been through hell but I'll be alright". 

I had surgery in March. Both breasts removed. My mom died while I was still recovering. I've not properly mourned her bc I'm dealing with my own personal hell at the moment. I finished 30 radiation treatments. My hair is thinning. Thanks to the radiation treatments I no longer grow underarm hair so, hey, glad I never paid for laser hair removal. Still not having to shave legs very often bc the hair doesn't grow there anymore. Yes, I'm counting small victories. 

Radiation was tough. 30 treatments. 5 days a week. The upper half of my body is now tanned while the lower half remains pale and that's ok. I'm dealing with mild lymphedema, a known possibility due to having lymph nodes removed. It's not terrible and I'm being proactive in managing it so that it doesn't become a big problem. 

Tomorrow I go back on the hormone therapy that made me so sick and I'm dreading it. I ran the numbers for my 5 year survival with and without those meds. It was significant enough for me to decide I'll do it. I'm thinking of what kind of legacy I want to leave my daughters and I want it to be that I'm a fighter. That I did not give up. I cannot leave a legacy of giving up bc it's hard. I can do hard things and when I'm gone they will remember their mom fought hard and did hard things. They are my daughters and they can do hard things too. That will be my legacy to them. 

Cancer has taken body parts. It has taken my joy. It has taken my ability to do the things I love but it will not take my legacy from my daughters. 

I'm not really paying attention to much wrt politics. I have limited time and I'm not going to spend it arguing with idiot fascists and lame politicians that are only out for themselves. 

I hope you all are doing well. This is the day the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it. 

That's it. I'll be back around in a few months and see how things are going on PDW. You're all still my people and I'm thankful for that.
